Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:10:1.hebrew: אלא - הכי פריך: ספק בכור לר"מ, אי בעלים חשודים עליה — נמצאו ישראל חשודים על ספק בכור, וכ"ש כהנים; דהא אי הוה נמי בבהמות עדר כהן ספק בכור הנולד בעדרו — בעי אמתוני עד שיומם, דכהנים לא נפטרו מבכור בהמה טהורה בפרק שני (לעיל בכורות יג.). וא"כ, מי מעיד עליו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:10:1.english: Rather - This is what [the Gemara] is asking: [Regarding] an animal of uncertain firstborn status according to Rabbi Meir, if the owner is suspected regarding it, it turns out that Israelites are suspected regarding an animal of uncertain firstborn status, and all the more so priests; for even if there were, among the animals of a priest's flock, an animal of uncertain firstborn status born in his flock, he must wait until it develops a blemish, as priests were not exempted from [the laws of] the firstborn of a kosher animal, [as stated] in the second chapter (above, Bekhorot 13a). And if so, who can testify about it?

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:11:1.english: [It] has no remedy - According to Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:11:2.hebrew: שחליפיו ביד כהן - כגון האי ספק בכור שהכהן נטל (את אחיו), פטור ישראל מן המתנות — דזרוע ולחיים וקיבה — דעשו שאינו זוכה כזוכה, כדאמרן בפרק שני (שם יח.). ור"מ מחייב — ומדמחייב ליה רבי מאיר במתנות, מכלל דבר אכילה הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:11:2.english: Whose replacements are in the possession of a priest - For example, this animal of uncertain firstborn status where the priest took (its brother): an Israelite is exempt from the gifts — of the foreleg, the cheeks, and the abomasum — because they treated one who does not acquire as one who acquired, as we said in the second chapter (ibid. 18b). “And Rabbi Meir deems [him] obligated” — and since Rabbi Meir obligates him in the gifts, it follows that it is an item [fit] for consumption.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:13:1.hebrew: הלכה כר"ש - דאפילו בנו ובתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:13:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel] - That even his son and his daughter [may testify].

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:14:1.hebrew: כהן בעליו - של בכור עמנו עומד בחוץ, ונכנס הבכור שלם בבית ויצא חבול — מעידין עליו אותם שבבית שמאליו נפל בו. אלמא, אין נחשד אלא כהן בעל הבית שהבכור שלו, כר"ש:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:14:1.english: The priest, its owner - [that is, the owner] of the firstborn, was standing outside with us, and the firstborn entered the house unblemished and emerged injured — those who were in the house may testify about it that [the blemish] occurred to it of its own accord. Evidently, no one is suspected except for the priest, the master of the house, whose firstborn it is, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:14:2.hebrew: אימא כל בעליו - בניו ובני ביתו עומדין עמנו בחוץ, ומעיד עליו רועה שהיה בבית:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:14:2.english: Say: All its owners - His sons and the members of his household were standing outside with us, and a shepherd who was in the house testifies about it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:15:1.hebrew: פשיטא - הואיל וכל בעליו עמנו, מי יטילנו כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:15:1.english: [It is] obvious - Since all of its owners are with us, who would inflict [a blemish upon] it, etc.?

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:15:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא ניחוש לחשדא - דרועה גופיה הטילו בו. ל"א: אימא כל בעלים עמנו, כלומר, אי אמרי סהדי: כל בעליו של בכור — דהיינו הוא ובני ביתו — היו עמנו בחוץ, ונכנס הבכור שלם בבית ויצא חבול, מעידין — כלומר, עדותן עדות ושרי, הואיל ולא היה איש בבית. ניחוש לחשדא — שמא הם גרמו לו מתחלה, שהניחו לו דבילה על האזן, אי נמי עשו לו גומא ונפל שם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:15:2.english: Lest you say we should entertain a suspicion - That the shepherd himself inflicted [the blemish] upon it. Another explanation: Say: “All the owners [were] with us” — that is to say, if witnesses say: “All the owners of the firstborn — that is, he and his household members — were with us outside, and the firstborn entered the house unblemished and emerged injured,” they may testify; that is to say, their testimony is [valid] testimony and [the animal] is permitted, since there was no person in the house. [Lest you say] we should entertain a suspicion — perhaps they caused it beforehand, in that they placed a pressed fig upon its ear, or alternatively, they made a pit for it and it fell there.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:1:1.hebrew: מימר אמר לא שביק - האי ישראל כהן צורבא מרבנן ויהיב לי לדידי, דסתם רועה עם הארץ הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:1:1.english: He says: He will not forsake - This Israelite [will not forsake] a priest [who is] a Torah scholar and give [it] to me, for an ordinary shepherd is an unlearned person.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:1:2.hebrew: רועי כהנים - רועי בהמות של כהנים, אע"פ שהרועים ישראל, אין נאמנין להעיד על בכורו של רבו כהן, דחיישי' ללגימא. וכ"ש רועי כהן ובהמות של רבן כהן, אין נאמנין, דחיישינן לגומלין וללגימא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:1:2.english: Priest-shepherds - Shepherds of animals belonging to priests: even though the shepherds are Israelites, they are not deemed credible to testify about the firstborn of their master, a priest, as we are concerned about a swallow [of food]. And all the more so [if the] shepherds are a priest and the animals belong to their master, a priest, they are not deemed credible, as we are concerned about reciprocal favor and about a swallow [of food].

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:2:1.hebrew: על של חבירו - אכהן לכהן קאי, וקאמר דנאמן הכהן הרועה על של רבו, דלא חיישי' לא לגומלין ולא ללגימא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:2:1.english: With regard to that of his fellow - It refers to [the case of] a priest for [another] priest, and it means that the priest who is a shepherd is deemed credible with regard to [the firstborn] of his employer, as we are not concerned either about reciprocal [behavior] or about a swallow [of meat].

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:2:2.english: One who is suspect about the matter - Priests are suspect regarding firstborns.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:2:3.hebrew: לא דנו ולא מעידו - ופליג אדר' שמעון, דשרי אפי' כהן לכהן; ופליג אדתנא קמא, דאמר: רועי בהמות ישראל, ואפילו הן כהנים — נאמנין, והרועים כהנים — אין נאמנין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:2:3.english: Neither adjudicate nor testify - And [Rabbi Meir] disagrees with Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel], who permits even a priest [to testify] for [another] priest; and he disagrees with the First Tanna, who said: Shepherds of an Israelite's animals, even if they are priests, are deemed credible, whereas priest-shepherds are not deemed credible.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:4:1.hebrew: היינו ת"ק - דהאמר ת"ק נמי, דכהן אינו נאמן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:4:1.english: This is the first tanna - For the first tanna also said that a priest is not believed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:5:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דר' יהושע בן קפוסאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:5:1.english: There is [a difference] between them [with regard to the statement] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai:

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:5:2.hebrew: צריך שנים מן השוק - שנים כל שהן, ואפילו כהנים, אבל כהנים שבביתו — לא. ת"ק אית ליה דרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, דקאמר ת"ק: רועי כהנים, בין בי ישראל בין בי כהנים, כדפרישית טעמא — אין נאמנין, אבל כהנים דעלמא נאמנין, ואפילו אבכורות דכהנים, ולא חיישינן לגומלין אלא ברועה דקאי גביה וסבר: אעיד את רבי, והוא יעידני כשיתן לי ישראל בעלמא בכור. ור"מ לית ליה דר' יהושע לגמרי, דכיון דנחשדו כהנים על הבכור — לא דן ולא מעיד, אפילו כהן דשוק, ואפי' הבכור ביד ישראל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:5:2.english: Requires two from the marketplace - Any two [people], and even priests; but priests who are members of his household [may] not. The first tanna holds in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, for the first tanna says: Priests' shepherds, whether in an Israelite's house or in a priest's house — as I explained the reason — are not deemed credible; but other priests are deemed credible, and even regarding the firstborn animals of priests. And we are not concerned about reciprocity except in [the case of] a shepherd who stays with him and thinks: "I will testify for my master, and he will testify for me when an ordinary Israelite gives me a firstborn." And Rabbi Meir does not hold in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua at all; for since priests are suspect regarding the firstborn, [a priest] may neither judge nor testify — even a priest from the marketplace, and even [if] the firstborn is in the hands of an Israelite.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:6:1.hebrew: ואפי' בנו ובתו - ר"ש לטעמיה, דאמר: נאמן הוא על של חבירו, ואביו היינו נמי חבירו, דאין כהן נחשד אלא על של עצמו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:6:1.english: And even his son and his daughter - Rabbi Shimon [follows] his reasoning, as he said: He is trusted regarding that of another; and his father is also [considered] another, for a priest is suspected only regarding his own.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:6:2.hebrew: אפי' עשרה והן בני ביתו אין מעידין - אבל מן השוק, עד אחד נאמן; דלר' יהושע צריך שנים מן השוק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:6:2.english: Even ten, and they are members of his household, may not testify - But from the marketplace, a single witness is deemed credible; for according to Rabbi Yehoshua, two from the marketplace are required.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:7:1.hebrew: ספק בכור - דשל ישראל הוא, כגון רחלה שלא ביכרה וילדה שני זכרים, דאמרי' בפ"ב (לעיל בכורות יז.): אחד לו ואחד לכהן, ואת שלו הוי ספק — שמא יצא ראשון — וירעה עד שיומם, ואוכלו ישראל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:7:1.english: An uncertain firstborn - That it belongs to an Israelite, such as a ewe that had not previously given birth and gave birth to two males, as we say in the second chapter (above, Bekhorot 17a): One belongs to him and one to the priest, and that which is his is of uncertain status, lest it emerged first, and it must graze until it develops a blemish, and then the Israelite may eat it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:7:2.english: Requires two [people] from the marketplace to testify about it - That a blemish was not intentionally inflicted upon it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:8:1.hebrew: כר יהושע - דכי היכי דבכור בי כהנים בעי שנים מן השוק להעיד עליו, ה"נ ספק בכור ביד ישראל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:8:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - For just as a firstborn in the possession of priests requires two [witnesses] from the marketplace to testify about it, so too [in the case of] an uncertain firstborn in the possession of an Israelite.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:1.hebrew: ר"נ אמר - ספק בכור ביד ישראל, אפילו בעליו ישראל נאמן; דכהנים נחשדו על הבכורות ולא ישראל, ואפילו על ספק בכור שנאכל להם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:1.english: Rav Naḥman says - [With regard to an animal of] uncertain firstborn status in the possession of an Israelite, even its Israelite owner is believed; for priests are suspected regarding firstborns, but not Israelites — and even regarding [an animal of] uncertain firstborn status, which is eaten by them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:2.hebrew: דאי לא תימא הכי - אלא בעלים חשודים עליו, אם כן הוי ישראל חשוד על המומין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:2.english: As, if you do not say so - But rather [that] the owner is suspected regarding it, if so, an Israelite would be suspected regarding blemishes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:3.hebrew: מעשר לר"מ - מי מעיד על מומו? הא א"ר מאיר: החשוד על הדבר לעצמו אינו מעיד לאחרים, כדחזינן ר"מ פוסל אפילו כהנים דשוק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:3.english: [Animal] tithe according to Rabbi Meir - Who can testify about its blemish? Behold, Rabbi Meir said: One who is suspected regarding a matter for himself may not testify for others, as we see [that] Rabbi Meir disqualifies even priests from the marketplace.

Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:4.hebrew: מעשר - בתמיה: הא ודאי מהימן אפילו בעליו, דהא אי בעי הוי שדי ביה מומא בהיתר בכוליה עדריה קודם שיעשר, דאכתי לא קדשא חד מינייהו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 35b:9:4.english: [Animal] tithe - [This is asked] in astonishment: Surely even its owner is certainly trusted, for if he had wanted, he could have cast a blemish permissibly upon his entire herd before he tithed, as not [even] one of them had yet become sanctified.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:11:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דלית להו תקנתא כו' - הוה מצי למימר: דחלקנו בין חבר לעם הארץ, כר' יהושע דלקמן; וכן בסמוך דפריך: "כהני ה"נ דלא דייני דינא?". א"נ, ר' יהושע עצמו חוזר בו — דקא"ל לר"ג: "היאך החי יכול להכחיש את החי", ופירש שם בקונט' שרוצה לומר: ודאי אמרתי וחוזר אני בו. ומיהו מסתברא דמשום כבוד דר"ג הוא דקאמר הכי, כי ההיא דתפלת ערבית (ברכות דף כז:) שאמר כמו כן, אע"פ שלא היה חוזר בו מה שאמר תחלה רשות — דהכי פסק רב התם: הלכה כדברי האומר רשות:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:11:1.english: “And if you would say that they have no remedy, etc.” - [The Gemara] could have said that we distinguish between a ḥaver and an am ha’aretz, in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua below (36a); and likewise nearby, where [the Gemara] challenges: “Do priests also not administer justice?!” [it could have resolved the difficulty in this manner]. Alternatively, [the Gemara did not offer this distinction because] Rabbi Yehoshua himself retracted [his position], as he said to Rabban Gamliel: “How can the living contradict the living?” (36a), and [Rashi] explained there in the Commentary that he meant: “Certainly I said [so], and [now] I retract.” However, it is reasonable [to say] that he said this [only] out of respect for Rabban Gamliel, like that [incident] regarding the evening prayer (Berakhot 27b), where he similarly said [this phrase], even though he did not [actually] retract what he had originally stated, [namely,] that it is voluntary — for Rav ruled there that the halakha is in accordance with the statement of the one who says [it is] voluntary.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:12:1.hebrew: אלא לאו ש"מ בעלים מעידין עליו - תימה: ורב חסדא, דבעי לעיל שנים מן השוק בספק בכור בי ישראל, תקשי ליה לר"מ: מי מעיד עליו, כיון דישראל נמי חשידי? וי"ל, דהוה משני כדפרישית: דחלקנו בין חבר לע"ה. א"נ, יאמר רב חסדא: ספק בכור לא יחמיר ר"מ שלא יהו שנים מן השוק נאמנים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:12:1.english: Rather, is it not [to be] deduced from this that the owners testify about it? - [This is] astonishing: According to Rav Chisda, who required above two [witnesses] from the marketplace in [the case of] a doubtful firstborn in [the possession of] an Israelite, let it be difficult for him: According to Rabbi Meir, who may testify about it, since Israelites too are suspected? And one can say that he would answer as I explained [above]: that we distinguished between a chaver and an am ha’aretz. Alternatively, Rav Chisda could say: [In the case of] a doubtful firstborn, Rabbi Meir would not be [so] stringent that two [witnesses] from the marketplace should not be believed.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:15:1.english: "We should entertain a suspicion" - That they would suspect that perhaps one [member] of the household remained [inside].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:16:1.hebrew: כהני הכי נמי דלא דייני דינא - לרבא, דאמר בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין כז.): "אוכל נבילות להכעיס, שהוא רע לשמים, אינו חשוד להיות רע לבריות" — לא פריך מידי; אבל לאביי התם — פריך שפיר. ועוד יש לפרש לרבא: דמשמע ליה שיש לכהנים להיות כשרים לכל (זמן) דין שבעולם ולכל הוראה, כדכתיב (דברים כ״א:ה׳): "כל ריב וכל נגע". ועוד היה יכול להקשות: היאך מותר לאכול משחיטתו, והיאך כשרים על כל קרבנות כולם? ועוד, בלא בכור נמי יכול להקשות לרבי מאיר, מטעם דנחשדו כהנים על השביעית, כדאמרינן בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין כו.):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:16:1.english: Priests should also not administer judgment - According to Rava, who says in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a) that one who eats non-kosher meat out of defiance, who is bad toward Heaven, is not suspect of being bad toward [fellow] human beings, [Rav Pappa] poses no difficulty at all; but according to Abaye there, he poses a good challenge. And furthermore, one can explain [the challenge even] according to Rava, as it implies to him that priests ought to be fit for any judgment in the world and for any halakhic ruling, as it is written (Deuteronomy 21:5): “Every controversy and every stroke.” And furthermore, [Rav Pappa] could have asked: How is it permitted to eat from [a priest’s] slaughter, and how are [priests] fit for all the sacrificial offerings? And furthermore, even without [the case of] the firstborn, he could also have asked according to Rabbi Meir on the grounds that priests were suspected regarding the Sabbatical year, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26a).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:1:1.hebrew: מימר אמר לא שביק צורבא מדרבנן ויהיב לדידי - והא דאמר לעיל בסוף פרק ב' (בכורות דף יח:) בחצר בעל הבית ורועה כהן, דלר"ט אקנויי מקני ליה מקום בחצירו, ואפילו ר"ע לא פליג אלא משום דאית [ליה] פסידא לא מקנה [ליה] מידעם — התם איירי במכירי כהונה, או שאוהבו ורגיל ליתן לו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:1:1.english: He says: "He will not forsake a Torah scholar and give [it] to me" - And as for that which [the Gemara] said earlier at the end of Chapter 2 (Bekhorot 18b) regarding [the case of an animal in] the courtyard of the homeowner and the shepherd is a priest, that according to Rabbi Tarfon [the homeowner] certainly transfers ownership of a place in his courtyard to him, and even Rabbi Akiva disagrees only because [the homeowner] incurs a loss, [so] he does not transfer anything to him — there, it is dealing with [the homeowner's] priestly acquaintances, or where he is fond of him and is accustomed to giving [priestly gifts] to him.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:5:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי - דת"ק סבר כוותיה, דדווקא רועי כהנים, בין בי ישראל בין בי כהנים, אינם נאמנים, כדאמר טעמא; אבל שני כהנים מן השוק נאמנים. ולר"מ, אפי' שנים מן השוק אין נאמנין, דלית ליה כרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי; דקסבר ר"מ: החשוד על הדבר, לא דנו ולא מעידו. ושנים מן השוק דקאמר ר' יהושע בן קפוסאי — בכהנים איירי, דישראל אפילו חד מהימן. ולר"מ, כל היכא דאסור, אפי' שנים אין נאמנין, כדאמר בסמוך: ספק בכור, לר"מ מי מעיד עליו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 35b:5:1.english: "There is [a difference] between them [with regard to the statement] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai" - For the first tanna holds in accordance with his [opinion], that specifically priest-shepherds, whether in an Israelite's house or in a priests' house, are not deemed credible, as [the Gemara] stated the reason; but two priests from the marketplace are deemed credible. And according to Rabbi Meir, even two [priests] from the marketplace are not deemed credible, as he does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai; for Rabbi Meir maintains: "One who is suspected regarding a matter neither judges it nor testifies about it." And [as for] "two from the marketplace" that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai said — it is dealing with priests, for [regarding] an Israelite, even a single [witness] is deemed credible. And according to Rabbi Meir, wherever [one] is prohibited [from testifying], even two are not deemed credible, as [the Gemara] says nearby: [Regarding] an uncertain firstborn, according to Rabbi Meir, who may testify about it?
